input:
In this worked example, we consider a flat stainless steel wall with a thickness of 20 mm that separates two process streams, and the aim is to estimate the heat flux passing through the wall under steady one-dimensional conduction. The thermal conductivity of the wall material is 16 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, and the measured temperature difference across the wall is 399 K, so the hotter stream loses heat through the metal to the colder stream at a rate set by these quantities together with the wall thickness. Expressed in metres, the thickness is 0.020 m, and the conduction relation makes the flux proportional to the conductivity and to the temperature difference, and inversely proportional to the thickness, so that a thinner wall or a more conductive metal would pass a larger flux for the same imposed difference. Putting the stated values into the relation gives a heat flux of 319200 W m⁻². It is important to note that this figure is an estimate for the metal wall alone. Surface (film) resistances on the two faces of the wall have been excluded from the estimate, and including them would add resistance in series with the wall, so the flux calculated on the same overall basis would be lower than the figure obtained here. The result therefore describes conduction through the wall itself, under the stated conditions, and it should not be read as the flux for the complete path between the two streams, which would have to account for the films as well.

Two features of the result follow from the form of the relation itself. The flux acts in the direction from the hotter face towards the colder face, because the temperature difference that drives the conduction is imposed across the wall in that direction. The flux also responds in proportion to its drivers: a larger temperature difference across the same wall would produce a proportionally larger flux, while a wall of greater thickness, with every other quantity unchanged, would produce a smaller flux, in inverse proportion to the thickness.
target:
A flat stainless steel wall of thickness 20 mm separates two process streams. Thermal conductivity is 16 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ and the measured temperature difference across the wall is 399 K. The example estimates the heat flux through the wall for steady one-dimensional conduction. Expressed in metres, the thickness is 0.020 m. The conduction relation makes the flux proportional to the thermal conductivity and to the temperature difference, and inversely proportional to the thickness. A thinner wall, or a more conductive metal, passes a larger flux at the same temperature difference. Substitution of the stated values gives a heat flux of 319200 W m⁻². The estimate covers the metal wall alone. Surface (film) resistances at the two faces are excluded, and film resistance acts in series with the wall. Including the films lowers the flux calculated on the same overall basis. The figure therefore describes conduction through the wall itself under the stated conditions. The complete path between the two streams includes the films, and a flux for the complete path is a different quantity from the wall flux reported here.

The relation behind the figure has three parts. Thermal conductivity measures how readily the metal conducts heat. The temperature difference drives the conduction, and the flux acts from the hotter face towards the colder face. The thickness resists the conduction. Covariation follows the same relation. A larger temperature difference across the same wall gives a proportionally larger flux. A wall of a more conductive metal gives a larger flux at the same difference and thickness. A thicker wall gives a smaller flux, in inverse proportion to the thickness. The stated figure is checked against the relation in that form: thermal conductivity, temperature difference and thickness together fix the flux, and no other property of the two streams enters the wall calculation. Properties of the streams enter only through the films at the faces, and the films are excluded from the estimate. The wall figure and a figure for the complete path therefore answer different questions, and the two are not interchanged.
